issues.description: Method inconsistency for Lecture.addGuestStudents: the problem statement (task description and UML) specifies addGuestStudents(int, String): void — i.e. two parameters: an int and a String reason (see problem_statement.md lines 49 and 73). The solution implementation in solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java declares public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) (single int parameter) at line 90. The template only contains a TODO and does not declare a concrete signature. This mismatch in parameter lists (presence/absence of the String reason) will confuse students about the API they must implement and may cause tests or expected usage to diverge.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method signature consistent across artifacts. Option A (preferred for pedagogy): update the template and solution to implement the two-parameter signature public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, String reason) and either store, log, or otherwise document the reason parameter so it is used or intentionally ignored with a comment. Update the solution implementation to add the new parameter (e.g., increment numberOfGuestStudents by numberOfNewGuestStudents and record or print the reason). Option B: if the reason parameter is not intended, update the problem statement and UML to require addGuestStudents(int): void and adjust the textual tasks to remove the String reason. Ensure the template, UML, problem text, and solution all use the exact same signature so students have a single unambiguous API to implement.
